parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented border/screening rule, no facility or custody exclusion, and no organised targeting appear in the dossier — the visitor carries no documented universal-exposure measure. But the negatives are real: no broad anti-discrimination law (2015 bill stalled), LGBT violence and discrimination described as frequent and 'often ignored by police' (thin recourse, tier 3), official hostility (2017 school discussion ban, book-burning rhetoric, Church/fundamentalist influence), no legal recognition and two trans migrants denied documents. Positives are thin but documented: same-sex conduct legal since 1990, health-sector social-name resolution, 2022 mental-health non-discrimination article, pride marches since 2004. No documented remedy working for trans visitors; feminicide and marriage figures are not trans-specific. Result: hostile climate with weak recourse but no state-imposed universal exposure — mid-scale.
